title: Capacity Telemetry Contract and Retention Spec
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary

This document defines the telemetry contract for capacity-related signals, the retention and sampling policy used for incident forensics and SLO validation, and the operational runbook for preserving and validating telemetry during incidents that affect capacity, SLOs, or error budgets. It applies to all runtime components that contribute to inference capacity, scheduling, and admission control (redwood-runtime, admission-proxy, batch-scheduler, cost-router).

Goals

- Provide a single source-of-truth for what capacity telemetry we collect, how long we keep it, and how it maps to SLIs and SLOs.
- Ensure incident responders can reliably reconstruct events that impact SLOs and error budgets.
- Balance storage and query cost against forensic fidelity by prescribing sampling and aggregation rules.
- Standardize change process for telemetry producers and consumers.

Scope

- Services in scope: redwood-runtime, admission-proxy, batch-scheduler, capacity-orchestrator, kvcache-service.
- Signals covered: request ingress, token consumption, scheduling decisions, queue latencies, GPU utilization, model load/unload events, eviction actions, throttles, admission rejections.
- Not covered: application-level domain telemetry (customer business events).

Telemetry Contract (primary metrics)

The table below is the canonical contract. Metric names are Prometheus-style. For each metric we specify description, producer, default scrape/emit frequency, retention class, aggregation used for SLIs, and primary owner.

| Metric name | Description | Producer | Emit frequency | Retention class | SLI aggregation | Owner |
|-------------|-------------|----------|----------------|-----------------|-----------------|-------|
| inference_requests_total | Count of requests received (per route/model/token-mode) | admission-proxy | 10s counter | hot (30d full-fidelity) | rate(1m) per token | eng-sre/runtime |
| inference_tokens_consumed | Tokens generated+consumed (per request) | redwood-runtime | 10s counter | hot (30d) | sum over 5m | eng-sre/runtime |
| request_queue_time_ms_p50/p90/p99 | Queue wait time before scheduling | batch-scheduler | histogram (10s) | warm (90d aggregated) | p99 over 1h | eng-sre/scheduling |
| gpu_utilization_pct | GPU utilization percentage (per host/pool) | gpu-fleet-agent | 10s gauge | warm (90d aggregated) | avg per 5m | eng-sre/gpu-fleet |
| admission_rejections_total | Requests rejected due to quota/overload | admission-proxy | 10s counter | hot (30d) | rate(5m) | eng-sre/runtime |
| prefix_kvcache_hit_ratio | KV cache hit ratio (per model, per pool) | kvcache-service | 10s gauge | warm (90d aggregated) | ratio over 5m | eng-sre/kvcache |
| model_load_time_ms | Time to load model weights into memory | model-manager | event | cold (365d sampled) | max per load | eng-platform/model-onboarding |
| eviction_events_total | Number of eviction actions (per host/pool) | capacity-orchestrator | event | hot (90d full-fidelity) | count per 1h | eng-sre/capacity |

Retention classes and rules

- Hot (full-fidelity, raw samples): 30 days. Used for live SLO debugging, billing reconciliation, and immediate post-incident forensics.
- Warm (aggregated, downsampled): 90 days. Aggregations include 1m and 5m rollups for counters and quantile summaries for histograms.
- Cold (sampled events): 365 days. Only critical events (model_load_time, eviction_events, admission_rejections with reason tag) are persisted; raw request traces are sampled at 0.1% by default unless flagged for preservation.

Sampling rules

1. Default request trace sampling: 0.1% across production tenants, biased toward large token requests (token_count > 5k) and high-cost models (labels: quantized=false, model_family in [gptx, redwood-3b]).
2. Preserve traces that trigger an SLO breach alert: increase sampling to 100% for a rolling 2 hour window for affected tenants/models.
3. If eviction_events_total increases by > 3x baseline in 15 minutes for a pool, preserve all admission_rejections and 10% of request traces for 7 days.

SLO and Error Budget mapping

- SLO names map to primary SLIs which are computed from the telemetry contract. Example:
  - SLO: inference-99-latency (p99 <= 300ms for route /v1/generate, monthly).
  - Primary SLI: request_total with request_latency histogram for route=/v1/generate.
- Error budget policy: when a monthly rolling burn rate > 2x for 1 hour, trigger the automated mitigation policy (see Mitigation & Throttle section below) and preserve full-fidelity telemetry for 72 hours.

Alerting thresholds (examples)

- SLO-breach-warning: p99 latency > 200ms for 15m -> paging to oncall if sustained.
- Emergency capacity alarm: GPU pool free_slots < 5% and admission_rejections_total rate > 10/s for 10m -> page oncall and capacity on-call.
- Telemetry pipeline health: metrics_exporter_error_rate > 0.5% for 5m -> page infra-observability.

Forensics preservation runbook (immediate steps)

1. Incident triage engineer (oncall) marks affected pool/route in the Incident Board and sets preservation flag via /internal/telemetry/preserve API.
2. System behavior: preservation flag causes telemetry backends to increase request trace sampling to 100% and extend hot retention to 90 days for affected keys.
3. Run these checks (commands):
   - kubectl -n runtime logs deployment/redwood-runtime --since=2h | grep "evict" | tail -n 200
   - promql: increase(admission_rejections_total[15m]) / increase(inference_requests_total[15m])
   - Clickhouse: SELECT * FROM request_traces WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND ts > now()-interval '2 hour' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 200;
4. If telemetry pipeline is degraded, follow Telemetry Failure Procedure (below).
5. Attach preserved traces and aggregated metrics to the incident ticket for postmortem analysis.

Telemetry failure procedure (if exporters or storage are down)

- Symptoms: slow or missing metrics, exporter error rate > 0.5%, or delayed rollups.
- Immediate actions:
  1. Verify exporter processes: ps aux | grep metrics-exporter on affected hosts. Restart exporter service if needed: systemctl restart redwood-metrics-exporter.service.
  2. If Prometheus scrape targets unreachable, switch to backup scrape target: run playbook/telemetry/switch-to-backend.sh --backend=prometheus-readonly.
  3. If storage (clickhouse) write lag > 10s, enable write-buffering mode and increase sampling to 0.05% to preserve pipeline: curl -XPOST /internal/telemetry/adjust-sampling -d '{"sampling":0.0005}'.
  4. Page observability team if storage errors persist > 10m.

Data schema examples (simplified)

1) Request trace (JSON event) stored in trace-store (fields):
   - trace_id, ts, tenant_id, route, model, token_count, tokens_generated, status, latency_ms, scheduling_delay_ms, gpu_host, cost_estimate_usd, tags

   Example:
   {
     "trace_id": "abcd-1234",
     "ts": "2026-02-10T14:12:03Z",
     "tenant_id": "tenant-42",
     "route": "/v1/generate",
     "model": "redwood-7b",
     "token_count": "1532",
     "tokens_generated": "1490",
     "status": "ok",
     "latency_ms": "284",
     "scheduling_delay_ms": "32",
     "gpu_host": "g-pool-03-12",
     "cost_estimate_usd": "0.0041",
     "tags": "quantized=false,priority=standard"
   }

2) Aggregated metric rollup (5m) stored in metrics-store (CSV row):
   - window_start, route, model, requests, tokens, p50, p90, p99, evictions, admission_rejections

Operational considerations and cost control

- Hot retention is expensive. To control cost:
  - Use targeted preservation (preserve only affected keys during incidents).
  - Implement cheap classifiers in admission-proxy to tag high-fidelity candidates (e.g., oversized requests) so sampling can be biased.
  - Periodically audit preserved datasets older than 45 days and downsample if not used for investigations.

Change process for telemetry producers

1. Proposal: author creates a telemetry change ADR describing new metric name, labels, cardinality estimate, intended consumers, and retention class.
2. Review: reviewers include eng-sre runtime owner, observability infra, and capacity team. 3 reviewers minimum.
3. Validation: new metric must include a backfill plan or default zero-value behaviour and a PromQL example for SLI calculation.
4. Deployment: feature flag the emitter; monitor exporter_error_rate for 24 hours.

SLI validation and regression testing

- Every SLO change must include an SLI validation checklist:
  1. Synthetic canaries generating traffic that exercise the SLI path.
  2. Shadow traffic mirroring for 72 hours with metric comparison script (diff tolerance 1%).
  3. A test incident run to verify preservation pipeline toggles are effective.

Owners and escalation

- eng-sre/runtime: primary owner for request and token metrics.
- eng-sre/capacity: owner for eviction, admission, and capacity orchestration signals.
- eng-platform/model-onboarding: owner for model load metrics.
- infra-observability: owner for telemetry pipeline and storage.

Escalation matrix (who to page first)

1. Oncall SRE (runtime) — page if SLO warning or evidence missing.
2. Capacity oncall — page if GPU pool free slots < 5% or evictions spike.
3. Observability infra — page if exporter/storage errors persist > 10m.

Appendix A — Example PromQL queries

- p99 latency for route /v1/generate over last 15m:
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[15m])) by (le))

- Admission rejection rate (per second) for the last 5m:
  increase(admission_rejections_total[5m]) / 300

- Eviction spike detector (true if >3x baseline):
  (increase(eviction_events_total[15m]) / (avg_over_time(increase(eviction_events_total[30d])[30d:15m]))) > 3

Appendix B — Preservation API examples

- Preserve key for 72 hours (curl):
  curl -X POST "https://internal.redwood/api/v1/telemetry/preserve" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"keys": ["pool:g-pool-03","route:/v1/generate"], "duration_hours": 72}'

- Query preserved traces (clickhouse):
  SELECT trace_id, ts, tenant_id, latency_ms FROM trace_store WHERE preservation_flag=1 AND ts > now()-interval '72 hour' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1000;

Maintenance and review cadence

- Quarterly review of hot retention sets and cost impact (eng-sre + infra-observability).
- Annual retention policy review with legal and security for compliance requirements.

Revision history

- 2025-09-15: Draft created (Ava Martinez).
- 2025-11-02: Added eviction sampling rules (reviewer: Priya Rao).
- 2026-02-10: Published with preservation API examples and PromQL additions (reviewers: Liam O'Connor, Marco Silva).
